name: WebAuthn passkey registration
plain: Creates a passkey or security key credential for the site.
meaning: Makes a public key login bound to the site's domain. The site never sees the private key or biometrics.

access.prompt_ui: OS or browser sheet: use Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello, phone or security key
access.persistence: Credential persists on authenticator or cloud keychain
access.revocation: Delete passkey in OS password manager; signalUnknownCredential from the site
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Creates a passkey or security key credential for the site.

fields.name: response.attestationObject
fields.range: format: none, packed, tpm, android-key, apple, fido-u2f

limits.headline: Can create a passkey or security key login for one site
limits.user_action: You tap Create a passkey and confirm with your fingerprint, face, phone or key
can: Ask your device to make a new key pair tied to that site
Save the public half on its servers so you can sign in later
Let you use a phone or a USB security key instead
cannot: See the private key; it stays on your device or password manager
Get your fingerprint or face data
Use that passkey on another site

story.what_it_is: Makes a new passkey for a site, tied to its domain.

marketing.name: Passkeys
marketing.pitch: Apple presents creating a passkey as saving a Face ID or Touch ID login that syncs across devices.

marketing.name: Passkeys
marketing.pitch: Google sells passkeys as sign in with your fingerprint, face or screen lock, saved in your account.

marketing.name: Web Authentication API
marketing.pitch: Describes a way for sites to sign people in with public key credentials held on a device, instead of passwords.

story.for_you: A prompt says something like 'Save a passkey for this site?' and you confirm with your face, fingerprint or PIN. After that you can skip the password. The site never sees your fingerprint or face.
story.for_makers: Makers get a safe way to sign people in without a password database to leak. It cuts reset support and stops phishing, and it is a selling point for security minded customers.

use_cases.example: A console or game account site invites a player to create a passkey after sign in, so a stolen password cannot take over the account.
A bank prompts a customer to add a passkey to replace text message codes.
A store offers 'Create passkey' on the order confirmation page so the next purchase is faster.
A code host or work app asks a new user to create a passkey in their password manager.
A payments app uses a new passkey to bind the browser as a trusted device for transfers.
A security team grows passkey enrollment as a measure of fewer account takeovers.

risks: Lose the device, lose the passkey if not synced

technical_bounds: Credential is bound to rpId; phishing sites cannot reuse it
Cannot read private key or biometric data
Attestation shown to the site only if user consents; most browsers default to none
Needs HTTPS (or localhost) and a user gesture on most browsers
